sentences.text: Fog forms when air cools to its dew point.
Advection fog forms when warm, moist air moves over cooler water, and it can persist for hours or even days.
In Florida, it’s most common in winter and spring, when warm air flows over cooler nearshore water.
Radiation fog forms on clear, calm nights as the land cools, and it can drift over rivers, bays and harbors until the morning sun burns it off.
When visibility drops, follow Rule nineteen: slow to a safe speed, turn on your navigation lights, sound fog signals, plot radar targets and post an extra lookout.
